# dsh-session-flags
Colored, user-named flags for DeepSeek Harness session lists.
Mark the sessions that matter, give each color a name of your own, and find them again from a search
hat matter, give each color a name of your own, and find them again from a searchable sidebar panel.
English | 中文
A flag is not a pin: pins reorder the list, flags label it. Use one color for “waiting on me”, anoth
er for “refactor in progress”, a third for “read tomorrow” — and rename the colors to match your own
factor in progress”, a third for “read tomorrow” — and rename the colors to match your own workflow.
## Highlights
- **A flag on every flagged session row.** A small flag glyph sits in the session-row leading seat,
right before the title, while the row is idle; the row's own status dot takes precedence when a sess

ion needs attention.
- **One click on hover.** The row's hover strip carries a flag button; its holl

ow state tells unflagged rows apart at a glance.
- **A “Set flag” row in the session “…” menu.** It

sits between “Fork” and “Archive” and previews the current color.
- **Named colors.** Each of the ei
ght palette colors can be renamed. Names show up in the hover card, the picker, and the menu, so the

color system can carry your own vocabulary.
- **A searchable “Flagged sessions” panel.** A sidebar
panel row opens a page that groups every flagged session by color, shows each color's name, and jump

s straight back to the conversation. Search matches session titles, workspaces, and color names.
- *

*Bilingual UI** (English / Simplified Chinese) following the GUI language.
- **Durable, local, priva
te.** Flags live in one JSON document under the DSH home, owned by the plugin's Host half. No networ
k calls, no telemetry, no changes to the sessions themselves.

## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness Desktop (or the Web GUI) **0.2.1-rc.2**. The package declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.

2.0-rc.2"`, and named installs are checked against that range before the package manager runs.
- The
plugin is a normal independent DSH plugin package (Host half + Client browser bundle); it installs
into a profile, not into the application.
## Install
### From npm
Published as the unscoped npm package `dsh-session-flags`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
In the GUI this is **Plugins → Add plugin**, typing `dsh-session-flags`. Either way, reload the prof
ile afterwards — restart the Harness so the new Client bundle is registered. On the official DSH Des
ktop app prefer the app's own **Settings → Plugins** page: that profile belongs to the app's plugin
manager, and the CLI cannot change it while the app is running.
### From a local checkout
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart the Harness and open the **Plugins** page — the bundle and its `dsh-session-flags` row shoul
d be enabled. The profile patch layer (`cordis.patch.yml`) is applied automatically through the pack
age's `dsh.bundle.patch` field.

## Marketplaces
Third-party listings are independent of npm. The community **dsh-market** reads the curated awesome-
dsh-plugin registry; a listing is one pull request that adds `data/plugins/<owner>__<repo>.yml`, and
the market app picks the entry up from that registry (usually within a day of the PR merging). The
exact submission file and release checklist are in docs/releasing.md.
The official Harness ships **no plugin market**. Its optional *custom plugin markets* bundle (`@deep
seek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle`) adds a **Discover** tab where the user adds market i
ndex sources; the community catalog is published as a format-1 index at `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/np
m/dsh-plugin-catalog/index.json`. Turn it on from **Plugins → More → Experimental plugins → Custom p
lugin markets**, add that source, and search for `dsh-session-flags`. With the bundle on, the agent
can browse the same indexes through the read-only `plugin_market` tool.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Host half** (`name` / `inject` / `apply`). It needs only `ctx.connection` and registers three exac
t Fetch routes below `/api/dsh-session-flags` (`state`, `set-flag`, `color-names`) with `ctx.connect
ion.fetch.register`. Each response uses the Connection convention `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: fa
lse, error: { code, message } }`. The document is persisted atomically (write temp file + rename) wi
th serialized mutations, so concurrent UI actions cannot lose a write.
**Client half.** It registers a locale namespace, one `<style data-plugin-css>` element, and six slo
It registers a locale namespace, one `<style data-plugin-css>` element, and six slot contributions:
| Slot | Entry |

| `sidebar.session.row.leading` | `FlagMark` — colored glyph in the leading seat |
| `sidebar.sessio

n.row.hover` | `FlagHoverTag` — dot + name in the hover card |
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.row.act

ion` | `FlagRowAction` — flag button in the hover strip |
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` |

`FlagMenuItem` — “Set flag” menu row |
| `shell.overlay` | `FlagDialog` — picker + color-name manag

er |
| `sidebar.panellist` | `FlagPanelIcon` — sidebar row for the flagged-session panel |
All six are registered through `ctx.slots.inject`, so they appear when the owning slot declares itse
lf and are disposed with the plugin. State flows through two observable sources (`FlagsStore`, `Dial
ogStore`) handed to the framework as `hooks`, which yields typed `useFlags(selector)` / `useDialog(s
elector)` hooks in every seat — no cross-slot imports.
**The panel** is a seventh contribution: a keyed entry in the layout's `main` slot under the panel i
d `dsh-session-flags`. The sidebar row and the page share that id (a panellist list id addresses the
matching main panel). The page reads the Session and Workspace Controller snapshots through the fra
mework's standard selector hooks, projects them plus the flag document with `buildFlagPanel` (pure,
unit-tested), and navigates by delegating to the Workspace UI service (`uiWorkspace.openSession`). T
hat service is injected through `ctx.inject`, so profiles without the workspace UI still keep every
row-level flag feature.
